text: Wish you a Happy New Year! May you turn a new leaf and become a valuable, positive, happy, tranquil, and energetic human being – stand proud as the great warrior of truth and happiness, ready to strike down anything negative!
author: Sri M

text: The secret of implementing a resolution is as the great Kabir Das said many hundred years ago: ' kal karey so aaj kar, aaj karey so ab …', which means 'What you are supposed to do tomorrow, do it today; and what you need to do today, do it right now!' There is no other way!
author: Sri M

text: Choose your goal carefully. Do that this New Year! Choose your goal! Don’t have too many goals – three or four goals do not work. Have one goal and stick to it, may you have all success!
author: Sri M

text: Any resolution has to be specific. If you resolve to be happy, have happiness as your aim – and sacrifice everything else for happiness. Happiness is attained by being good and ‘Letting Go!’
author: Sri M

text: ‘Let go’ doesn’t mean ‘giving up’ throw everything and run away to the cave! It means - Let go of all the unpleasant memories, the hurts, the wounds, the bitterness that's in your mind – let it all go.
author: Sri M

text: Let go and rejoice – let none of your hurts and negativities stick to you. Throw them away – let go of them. Then, be free and rejoice in the bliss of the tranquil mind which is at the core of your being. That’s the secret of happiness!
author: Sri M

text: WRITE DOWN YOUR GOAL. Every night, before you go to sleep, take the slip, read it again and again. Repeat it like a mantra. Believe me, if you are serious and sacrifice time and energy, the mind will find ways and means to bring about situations to fulfill the aim. This is true, as imagination is a gift from the Divine.
author: Sri M

text: Patanjali says the only way to make the mind one-pointed and free from agitation is dīrgha kāla nairantarya meaning ‘Practice, practice, practice for a long, long time’ – this is the only way to implement your resolution; to clear up your mind; to make it positive.
author: Sri M

text: A small good deed, a kind deed done to another human being or another living creature, can wipe out the dirt of negativity that has gathered in your soul and make it free and clear as a mirror to reflect Divinity.
author: Sri M

text: Let us resolve to do the best we can to help at least one unfortunate human being this year, let go of all negativity, of all hatred and anger in us from last year and rejoice in the goodness and happiness, peace and brotherhood of the whole world.
author: Sri M

text: Initially dharana is possible for most, only for a short period. When this dharana, through practice and proper guidance becomes continuous, the exclusive fixing of attention on one, and remains for a long period without distraction then it is called dhyana.
author: Sri M

text: Experiencing life through the sorrows and the pleasures, the pains and the happiness that the body and the mind go through, one evolves into a better and cleaner entity before it touches a level that cannot even be called human, but divine.
author: Sri M

text: Have patience in the face of criticism. Even when greatly agitated, try to be patient. Things will take care of themselves.
author: Sri M

text: When you sit for long periods before a Dhuni and meditate, it is about you contemplating on the outer fire - an act that helps to light the inner fire.
author: Sri M

text: In the language of Yoga, our flute is the spine and it is usually full of muck.. One cannot do anything more; only clean it up and wait! He will sing only when He wants to. One can only wait.
author: Sri M

text: It is possible to live in this world and reach one’s spiritual fulfillment at the same time, provided we know the rules, regulations and the traffic signals to watch out for. We can then use this world as a finishing school to graduate into the higher realms of consciousness.
author: Sri M

text: When you go to a cave to meditate, you can leave everything behind but remember you take your mind with you. Yes! The problem is the mind and not the material things around you.
author: Sri M

text: Nobody can give us illumination; we have to find it ourselves. Just as one who is hungry has to find food for oneself.
author: Sri M

text: The greatest miracle is having the ability to lead a person to spiritual growth. Beyond that, there is no bigger miracle, and it is the most challenging miracle possible.
author: Sri M

text: When you are alone, that's the only time you are really with yourself. Then, you get to see your mind and how you relate to other people. There are amazing levels of consciousness you can be aware of when you are alone.
author: Sri M

text: The only way to find the Truth is to take the images or expectations out of our minds.
author: Sri M

text: In the spiritual sphere, we miss the obvious because we desire for the exotic.
author: Sri M

text: Spirituality is a beautiful breeze, moving grass, tranquil mountains, sitting quietly and hearing the church bells toll. Once one settles down, you will find that it also happens within.
author: Sri M

text: Examine yourself in the morning when you wake up and in the evening before you go to sleep. And see – have I changed or am I the same or worse? Am I angry because somebody else is happy?
author: Sri M

text: Whatever be the situations, look at them carefully and try to work out how best you can handle them. In this regard, sadhana is a significant part of your daily life. Without practice, you cannot control these situations.
author: Sri M

text: A person who has touched that freedom, a person who has understood this freedom, moksha or mukti, this completeness, lives an unprejudiced life of total freedom not influenced by the stereotyped images that one encounters in day to day life.
author: Sri M

text: The avadhoot Dattatreya had twenty-four teachers in his life, and one of them was the honey–bee. He says,’ I learnt the lesson from the honeybee, collecting and storing for a rainy day’; how it goes from flower to flower, sucks the honey, and gathers it. This shows that there is nobody on this earth who knows everything!
author: Sri M

text: The world is such a funny place – you try to chase something and it always seems to run away from you. You leave it and it tries to follow you! It happens. When you don’t want it, it comes to you!
author: Sri M

text: The mind has to be kept lively, no matter the consequences - including physical age. There are ways and means to achieve this. One has to decide that you are not going to let yourself feel old within, look at life with an open mind; be vigilant, be agile.
author: Sri M

text: Sharing is an essential part of well-being. As you give, so you receive. So, give whenever possible, whatever possible, in whichever way you can.
author: Sri M

text: You need to practice. The approach does not matter. Results come with constant practice. This helps you maintain your spiritual journey without disruption. It’s not the terminology that matters, it’s what you do.
author: Sri M

text: If we are making spiritual progress, don’t judge by how many visions or lights one sees. What we have to look at is how one behaves. Have I become less selfish? Has my world narrowed down or has it expanded? Do I feel bad for the child next door or is it only for my child?
author: Sri M

text: If we have one mind, a change in one part should affect the other. So, if we change ourselves, that change will affect all.
author: Sri M

text: When one is established in deep silence, then no noise can disturb you. Silence is not the absence of sound. In the depths of your heart, there is silence. You sometimes come upon it when you look at the lake or the mountain.
author: Sri M

text: While personal understanding and guidance are essential, it is also important that one’s aspiration for spiritual knowledge is profound.
author: Sri M

text: If you are seeking a spiritual teacher, get rid of the conventional ideas you may have about a teacher, because that prejudice may prevent you from seeing a real teacher.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t just accept what someone says. The idea is to go within oneself. If one doesn’t go into one’s mind, one cannot comprehend the different layers of the mind, which generally creates all our problems.
author: Sri M

text: In general, we don’t look at ourselves, and we blame others because we are either not prepared or we don’t have the guts to open ourselves up to take a look. We are afraid we might be opening a ‘Pandora’s Box’.
author: Sri M

text: The Upanishads are here to help us find our true self. Find out for yourself. It’s the process of going deeper and deeper into one’s inner layers of consciousness.
author: Sri M

text: Looking within is not just sitting with one’s eyes closed. It means to watch your mind, to be watchful of your interactions in everyday life towards others. That's when you realize who and what you are.
author: Sri M

text: When emotions come, don’t run away from them. Feel what is happening. We cannot discover ourselves in a ‘dry’ emotionless manner. Only when we experience emotions, are we human beings.
author: Sri M

text: How does a person grow? Not by owning huge properties and great wealth but by beginning to think that everyone is important and essential.
author: Sri M

text: The greatest penance is to calmly and quietly hear someone insulting us with absolutely no reaction. And, at the end of it, to say ‘thank you very much’. That would be the highest penance for a yogi.
author: Sri M

text: Think outside the box. Don’t go solely on linear logic; use fuzzy logic. Turn things upside down and look, you will see things are quite different.
author: Sri M

text: Look at the Upanishads; nobody preaches anything there. They say - ‘Explore’!
author: Sri M

text: What we see in this world today is a result of the lopsided development of the frontal lobe. Due to this, so many other parts of the brain have been neglected. They lie latent and can be activated. It’s time now to evolve towards the spiritual.
author: Sri M

text: Sometimes what happens is we read so much of the scriptures that there is not enough space within to accommodate the understanding.
author: Sri M

text: Sleep is so rejuvenating because one is fully unaware then that they exist. The moment one knows, there is no rest. That’s when all the issues crop up. ‘I’ am the first problem. The problem starts with ‘Me’.
author: Sri M

text: No one can spiritually advance by simply sitting down cross-legged and meditating 24 hours. The moment you begin to see divinity in all living beings and start serving human beings, the mind can begin to purify and reach higher states. Service is an important part of Sadhana.
author: Sri M

text: When we meditate, we see that the mind wanders either because we are attracted to or repulsed by something. If this unrest is settled by the understanding that this is the cause of one not being empty and free, then it becomes easy to sit and meditate.
author: Sri M

text: We have to change first; we can’t change the world until we transform. Small drops make the ocean.
author: Sri M

text: Questions never end. When you figure out that questions are part of the movement of the mind, and everything is still, there is nothing left to ask. This is something that has to happen on its own; it’s not something that can be imposed on anybody.
author: Sri M

text: In each individual’s spiritual journey, the pace may differ. There are many influences and reasons, so one should never give up. Carry on!
author: Sri M

text: It’s the straight and narrow path. Start slow. Patience is very important. You should care how you live. Spiritual practice is not that you continue to live the way you do and practice in a mechanical way. You should also change your life. Only then, if you introduce a technique, it works.
author: Sri M

text: The paths are many, and the goal is total fullness and completeness. This is what we are all seeking though we may not be spiritually inclined. If even a few people understand this and start living this way, we can change the world.
author: Sri M

text: To be spiritual does not mean to become weak. Forgiveness is a great strength. It’s the weak who cannot forgive.
author: Sri M

text: Then all the desires of the heart have been understood and let go of, and when the spirit finds joy and satisfaction in itself without any external add-ons, then one is a person with steady wisdom.
author: Sri M

text: Running away from one’s circumstances is not the solution. When the mind is steady, the steadiness and wisdom are not dependent on external circumstances.
author: Sri M

text: There is an eternal element in all of us that is joyous by its very nature.
author: Sri M

text: When the love for the Divine arises, it’s like an overflow. There are no questions.
author: Sri M

text: Whether on the path of self-realization or not, you should think that things will happen at the right time. Keep working; patience is of the essence.
author: Sri M

text: Ideally, it’s good to erase one’s yesterday and live today. You are lighter; there are no burdens.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t go to extremes. If you go to one extreme in this world, you might get thrown to the other. Moderation is the key.
author: Sri M

text: Even if you touch a tiny part of what's inside - the real, conscious, bliss, Ananda - then you can sail through life because your treasure is within you. This treasure is the source of the entire universe.
author: Sri M

text: The greatest miracle for a great yogi is to guide someone to the Truth. If one person in a million reaches the highest, it's a great miracle.
author: Sri M

text: We all are actually ‘pashus’ although we think we are ‘manushya’, deep down we are all ‘pashus’, and Shiva is the Lord who presides over us, He is called Pashupathi.
author: Sri M

text: When Adinath dances his Tandav Nritya , he destroys images. He explodes all the images that we have created and nothing new can come up. Like death, He destroys the old, the stratified, the calcified and the fossilized!
author: Sri M

text: Shivam means consciousness, bliss, and auspiciousness. It is present within us and moving towards That is the spiritual journey.
author: Sri M

text: Shivaratri is a new beginning as He finishes his dance of destruction. Now, this dance of destruction is a very auspicious thing. The dance of destruction is actually a renewal, where the old is destroyed and the new takes place.
author: Sri M

text: When Buddha said to his monks - ‘Go Forth!’, he didn’t mean to only walk, he also meant getting out of the stagnant little pool that we have created for ourselves. Move!
author: Sri M

text: To begin one’s spiritual journey, the starting mind must be a quiet mind, a tranquil mind. It is a runway from which you can take off.
author: Sri M

text: Yoga is not a passive state. It is a super-active state wherein there's action in the tranquillity of mind, without agitation.
author: Sri M

text: If the body has not rested and is not alert, then it cannot meditate. It'll impact the mind. So, keep your body in a state where it's not tortured by lack of sleep or extreme fasting.
author: Sri M

text: Moderation in all areas - eating, drinking, sleeping, and also entertainment. But don’t make entertainment your sole aim in life.
author: Sri M

text: It doesn’t matter who the teacher is, what he or she looks like, etc. What's important is the wisdom that comes from the teacher.
author: Sri M

text: If we live in this world with the heart anchored to the core Truth, then we can live more efficiently than ever before.
author: Sri M

text: A spiritual seeker is not tempted by anything other than to find the truth one-pointedly.
author: Sri M

text: Is there some way by which the ordinary mind, caught up in this world with its pains and pleasures, be free and touch the essence? The study of this is called the Brahmavidya, and the way to do this is called Yoga.
author: Sri M

text: Yoga is not merely standing on your head. It’s much more. The true meaning of Yoga is the complete ending of the mind's distractions.
author: Sri M

text: All meditations essentially boil down to how to make the mind free of distractions, how to make it settle down, and finally how to remain in the eye of the storm, be completely free, and not be distracted by anything.
author: Sri M

text: Use your mind as the bow, your will as the bowstring, and ‘OM’ as the arrow. Aim at the Supreme Being and let go of the arrow one-pointedly.
author: Sri M

text: The mind is so limited that it cannot find Reality through thought. So, what do you do? Open the heart.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t think that meditation happens only when you sit cross-legged in one place. Meditation is any activity that brings about love, affection, calmness of mind, and tranquility leading to the ultimate goal.
author: Sri M

text: When you become more mindful of yourself, you become more mindful of the outer world.
author: Sri M

text: Music is an excellent help for meditation because it takes you away from the conditionings of language. Music is uniting, as opposed to the language that is sometimes dividing.
author: Sri M

text: The highest knowledge is that which leads you to the Truth.
author: Sri M

text: The theoretical aspect is one thing, and experience is another. Some people understand this Truth and become totally silent because it can’t be expressed in words.
author: Sri M

text: Some people have so much theoretical knowledge and are swollen with the ego of this knowledge that they begin to think they are spiritually illuminated and start teaching people. When they do that, it’s like the blind leading the blind.’
author: Sri M

text: The highest function of the intellect is to understand its limitations in the spiritual field. This is possible only if you have really good intelligence; good intelligence sharpened by concentration and one-pointed attention that is free from distractions of the world.
author: Sri M

text: No amount of bhajan or kirtan is of any use unless the heart changes and starts to look outside oneself. If we can spend even half an hour for others, then we are moving forward.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t unnecessarily complicate life with too many things. Speak the truth; More than speaking the truth, think the truth. That does not mean that when you speak the truth you have to be blunt. There are sweet ways of speaking the truth. You need not be brusque and suffer because of that.
author: Sri M

text: We always think that only happiness is a blessing. Sorrow is a blessing too. It leads us to greater, deeper, and more permanent happiness. Sometimes, sorrow is given particularly to a person who is on the path – to see how he or she is progressing.
author: Sri M

text: There is only One Supreme Being and that Supreme Being resides in the hearts of all. He is the Antaryami . By living a good life, praying, meditating, and trying to touch the Lotus Feet of this Being, who resides in your own heart, one can grow and attain great spiritual heights.
author: Sri M

text: What each one of us must understand is to first lead a good life by helping as many people as possible, to sing the name of God, to do our ‘japa’, and to dwell on the Inner Spirit constantly.
author: Sri M

text: Saburi means complete patience, especially in sadhana where one has to go through so many trials and tribulations.
author: Sri M

text: At least in spiritual matters, please don’t lie! Don’t say I meditated for six hours today and lights were going up and down. Say only what you really feel. If you don’t follow this, it is the greatest blunder that can happen.
author: Sri M

text: When you say ‘empty yourself,’ it could also mean - ‘empty yourself’ of your prejudices, of all ideas that have been put into your brain, of all preferences, of things that you instantly dislike and like because our sub-consciousness has been conditioned to certain things. Emptying all this is actually the process of Sadhana .
author: Sri M

text: If you look at life, it's in itself a miracle. You don’t need any other miracles.
author: Sri M

text: It's dangerous for spiritual aspirants to get caught up in miracles. Most of the miracles are of this world, and if you get caught up in it, you're also caught up in this world.
author: Sri M

text: Thinking itself is ‘mind’. When there are thoughts, automatically there is the mind. Therefore it implies that where there is no thought there is no mind, in the ordinary sense of the term.
author: Sri M

text: There is no difference in the ancient universal teachings. But when it becomes more organized, it loses its core. Why? Because we get more interested in the external aspects.
author: Sri M

text: Being truthful and honest is a prerequisite for any spiritual journey.
author: Sri M

text: Truth is infinite. So, there must be infinite ways of approaching it. Truth is like the sun; there is nothing secret about it. It is open to all, especially now when the human brain has evolved enough to look at it accurately.
author: Sri M

text: When you understand that the spiritual journey is not something dry but exciting and if you are genuinely interested in it, then you will have no distractions whatsoever. Until then, you have to keep bringing back your distracted mind to the journey.
author: Sri M

text: Whatever happens, even if you are sick, try not to miss the routine practice of meditation.
author: Sri M

text: The Gita is an exhortation to perform action and not to run away from it. It is not that one becomes inactive. One acts but is not caught by the results of the activity. This is karma yoga.
author: Sri M

text: An example of Karma Yoga is looking after someone who is not well, as you get nothing out of it. This act is Karma Yoga in its purest form.
author: Sri M

text: Usually, the mind is scattered; therefore, your energies are also scattered. To find out which is essential, you need to gather these energies together. Therefore, all the training of various schools is to make a mold in which all these broken pieces can be made into a specific shape. Once done, you break the mold.
author: Sri M

text: Anyone who has succeeded in stilling the disturbances and the subtle hankerings of the mind, and all the work that this person does is for others and not for oneself, then that person has already climbed ten steps towards the Science of Yoga.
author: Sri M

text: Layers of prejudice close the eyes, ears, and heart. When the wind blows, nothing can enter. So, all the practices we do are meant to open the windows to the heart.
author: Sri M

text: Ultimately, you are your own Master. There is no other. A teacher can help you understand this point. If you do, then you are free.
author: Sri M

text: There is a divinity in every heart, and that divinity - by its very essence - is peace, tranquility, and happiness. The more you tune into it, the happier you are, the better your mind is, and the better you function in your relationship with others.
author: Sri M

text: In the Bhagavad Gita, Krishna tells Arjuna that the mind can be a friend, but the same mind can also be an enemy. Cultivate the friendly side of your mind. And, don’t give too much attention to the enemy.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t be afraid of being left alone. When left alone, that's the time you can look into yourself and find out where your problems are. So, appreciate it when you are alone and be thankful to those who have let you be alone.
author: Sri M

text: Be practical. Go to the essence of the teachings of the Upanishads. Understand yourself. Everything that you need is in you. There is nothing outside. Be independent and wherever possible, be kind to others.
author: Sri M

text: While it is a good thing to cultivate positive thoughts and to keep negative thoughts at bay while moving on this spiritual field, you must also understand that from the pure point of spiritual understanding, there is no positive or negative thought. It is all thought. The more free you are from it, the better.
author: Sri M

text: It doesn’t matter what your belief system is. If you need to survive in this world, you need to put in hard work.
author: Sri M

text: No matter how different one is externally, the inner spark is not different, it is from the same source. The commonality is the inner, not the outer.
author: Sri M

text: Revolution is necessary, this is the ‘churning,’ what Shankaracharya says is ‘shad’ shaking up in the Upanishads. Shaking up of the mind is revolution’. It’s not just physical movement.
author: Sri M

text: There are two very important things we pray and meditate for - protection from the vagaries of nature and protection from thoughts that disturb me. I may be in a fortified house but my mind needs protection from distraction & conflict.
author: Sri M

text: Meditation means many things to many people. For instance, you could be alone sitting on the beach, looking at the sea and the waves and see how they go up and down, crash down and move forward. Your mind is now in a state of outer meditation with no unnecessary thoughts.
author: Sri M

text: The symbol of Hippocrates - A stick with two winged wands with two snakes intertwined - is similar to the three main nadis. The winged wand is the ‘Sushumna’ and the other two are the ‘Ida’ and the ‘Pingala’.
author: Sri M

text: Sankhya philosophy says that the subtlest part of the food we eat goes to make the mind. We need proper nourishment, physical as well as mental. Mind needs to be nourished with the right kind of living and understanding.
author: Sri M

text: If the mind can be free of distractions, if the mind can become tranquil, then it is able to access that fullness in us which is actually a spark of the universal fullness; and it's also blissful. It's that bliss that we seek when we try to find happiness here and there.
author: Sri M

text: There is a kind of state between sleep and wakefulness which is so blissful that one does not want to come out of it. When you are experiencing it, it’s meditation.
author: Sri M

text: Don't be obsessed with failure. All people who have succeeded are those who have failed and continued and said we will somehow do it.
author: Sri M

text: A Yogi’s mind is not a lethargic mind. It's an ever active, alert but tranquil mind. A spiritual being is one who keeps doing his work. A lazy mind is a devil’s workshop anyway.
author: Sri M

text: Unless your body and mind are healthy, you cannot reach That.
author: Sri M

text: When you are in natural settings, not man-made, it’s easier for the mind to be meditative. So, the closer you are with things that are not man-made, the mind expands and gets into a meditative state.
author: Sri M

text: By taking Sanyasa and joining an ashram full time, you think you will find peace? In a small group where there are very few people, politics becomes stronger. All the attitudes which one has lying underground, come up. Wherever you go, you take your mind.
author: Sri M

text: Constant happiness comes when the mind understands the Truth and says the essence of happiness is inside and not outside. This is the teaching of the Upanishads. This is the teaching of yoga. This is what the ancients have been saying for ages.
author: Sri M

text: The mind has subtle hankerings for so many things, you may change robes, you may shave your head but the mind does not change easily. You can be a yogi only when you can keep your mind quiet and tranquil without allowing it to run after objects.
author: Sri M

text: The ancients said that the fragrance that you seek is in you. You think it is outside but it is actually in you and that fragrance happens to be your true soul or your true identity, free of all other distractions.
author: Sri M

text: There are some people who seem to be happy in all situations. How? Because they have found out, through experiences of life that the peace, tranquility, and happiness that they seek is inside, not outside.
author: Sri M

text: When the mind is free of all distractions, when it settles down, tranquil and quiet, then you find the treasure trove of happiness within you.
author: Sri M

text: There is happiness temporarily because we have acquired something. My mind has stopped craving for it and it’s at rest. I think the object I have acquired has made me happy. Examine carefully. Even after you have acquired something, if there is no satisfaction, then there is no happiness.
author: Sri M

text: We always feel we are inadequate, we are incomplete, our search for happiness is for this completeness. The Vedas say that we are part of the Completeness which is all around us. We are unable to access it only because our minds are mostly in conflict & confusion. Can we keep our minds tranquil?
author: Sri M

text: For the yogi, praise and blame are equal. In pleasure or in pain, in heat or in cold, a yogi manages to keep his mind balanced.
author: Sri M

text: Revolution is necessary, this is the ‘churning,’ what Shankaracharya says is ‘shad’ shaking up in the Upanishads. Shaking up of the mind is a revolution’. It’s not just physical movement.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t depend on your happiness from anything outside. It’s nice to have things that make life convenient but don’t think that this is going to be the cause of your happiness permanently. The source of happiness is within us.
author: Sri M

text: Externally he may be a carpenter, a cook, or an Engineer. Only externally! But internally, if that person has seen the Divine in all hearts, he is never lost to the Divine because everywhere there is Divinity everywhere.
author: Sri M

text: ‘Who am I’ cannot be found out through chanting this continuously. It is an inquiry and not a chant. The inquiry is to find the witness in us who is present in all states - waking, dream, and deep sleep. The witness is the source of joy we feel in all experiences we go through.
author: Sri M

text: Krishna says what is called ‘sanyasa’ or renunciation is the same as Yoga, the discipline of selfless action. The more selfless an action becomes, the more one moves forward on the spiritual path.
author: Sri M

text: In ancient times, in the olden days, all householders had a fire in their house for homa. It’s called the Fire and it’s a ritual. It means lighting the Fire for offering thanks to the Creator. It also means the fire of the desire for spiritual fulfillment which is inside. The internal fire or Agni has to be kept burning.
author: Sri M

text: By meditative state, I mean that the mind breaks free from petty concerns that constantly make it chatter and settles down quietly into a wider expanse.
author: Sri M

text: The spiritual journey is not something passive. It requires prime energy. It’s not something that can be done when one has retired. It requires virility. When you go to a teacher, go with your fuel in your hand and be ready to utilize this in a useful way. Not burn it if off in useless actions.
author: Sri M

text: Swami Vivekananda said that one cannot meditate all the time. Serving humanity is needed. Moksha for the self and wellbeing of humanity was his motto.
author: Sri M

text: The first chapter of the Gita is called “ Arjuna Vishada Yoga ”, the yoga of Arjuna’s dissatisfaction, sorrow, and insecurity. It’s a study that is for all of us because we are not actually in the battlefield of Kurukshetra, but we all have this battlefield of life.
author: Sri M

text: In life, we go through all circumstances. Sometimes there is happiness, sometimes there is sorrow. Sometimes people blame you, sometimes they praise you. The yogi is one who considers praise and blame as equal. He is not moved by it.
author: Sri M

text: Conscious means to be aware of the world, of all that you see in the world; all these things together constitute consciousness. Consciousness naturally also means awareness.
author: Sri M

text: The Gita says Sanyasa is not throwing away things and walking off. It is when one can live under all circumstances without being attached to it. No change of robe, no nothing is required.
author: Sri M

text: Sometimes the aspiration for spiritual practice comes in the presence of someone who has touched it. You feel what is the secret of this person's happiness? He doesn’t seem to possess much, but he is very happy. What is this? So, then the inquiry comes - can I also touch this?
author: Sri M

text: The movement towards fulfillment and happiness is the whole center of civilization. All civilization has come because we want to expand, improve, become more refined and experience more happiness.
author: Sri M

text: Every little cell has an intelligence and therefore it is conscious. In every cell and in every living being there is intelligence, therefore, there is consciousness.
author: Sri M

text: If you can be mindful of your thoughts, actions, meditation, and breath, that is called mindfulness. Complete mindfulness is not just a small practice but a total mindfulness as you go along with life.
author: Sri M

text: We spend all our lives trying to push sorrow away and keep only happiness. This is not possible. The very moment you try to push sorrow away you create more sorrow. If you understand this, then even in sorrow you are ok. Because when there is happiness, there is bound to be sorrow.
author: Sri M

text: The true essence of Consciousness is beyond the brain but functions through the brain. If you have to touch That consciousness which is not part of the brain - with its activities, memories, emotions, and reaction, then perhaps, when that becomes still and quiet then you experience That consciousness which is other than merely the brain consciousness.
author: Sri M

text: The grace is always there. But our windows are closed and you can’t dictate when the grace should flow. The entire process of spiritual practice is to leave your windows and doors open, so when it comes, we don’t miss it.
author: Sri M

text: There is a constant movement towards trying to find peace by acquiring things but that never happens. That’s why the Upanishads say ‘Tena Tyaktena Bhunjita’; Let go and rejoice.
author: Sri M

text: Half an hour or one hour of sitting down quietly and being mindful of your mind, thoughts, and breath is a very important preparation to attain that mindfulness which we seek, which is to be totally free of all this.
author: Sri M

text: Can you conceive of a mind without thoughts, you cannot. So mind means thought and therefore if I say I am now tranquil and thoughtless, the thought is still there. All you can do is, as Patanjali said,” chitta vritti nirodha ”, get rid of the distractions of the mind.
author: Sri M

text: Sometimes spiritual inclination happens when you ultimately see the futility of all this. You feel it’s so false. People don’t mean what they say, and you have happiness but there is sorrow also lurking round the corner. You see this and say I should look into something that is beyond.
author: Sri M

text: Every mantra is not suitable for everybody, take time to choose. Once you have chosen, stick to it for some time till you begin to feel the effects of it.
author: Sri M

text: Consciousness is all-pervading, Purna – complete, which we cannot define and the brain is a product of evolution which has become so refined and functional that the consciousness is able to function through it in a beautiful way, in a great way like a man operating a very advanced computer.
author: Sri M

text: The world that we know is only an impression that the sense organs keep of an object in front of us. We really don’t know what the object is. We only know the impression of the object.
author: Sri M

text: From the yogic teachings, the flute of the Lord is the spine which is the central nervous system anatomically, the sushumna nadi with no muck, absolutely clean, and with seven holes to play the different tunes. It’s our flute which has to be emptied of all negativity, cleaned up, space created, and left surrendered to the music.
author: Sri M

text: When you come to the point that enquiry is the most important thing in your life, the urgency becomes so important that you say that this is what I really want. I don’t want anything else. author: Sri M

text: When we understand that perhaps consciousness is there even when the brain is not functioning, then probably we are touching That essence of consciousness. Once that is touched, you probably can operate even without the brain for some things; not for everything.
author: Sri M

text: One who has control over his senses and emotions. One who controls his mind, rather than runs after the mind, remains tranquil under all circumstances and one who has the concern of all living beings in his heart - are dear to Krishna as per Bhagwad Gita.
author: Sri M

text: If you watch your mind with complete attention and see how the thoughts come up when you meet people, when you react to what you read, when you see things, then you are being mindful of your mind: that is called mindfulness.

text: Because you are emotional, it doesn’t mean that you should not maintain tranquility. Your emotions should be directed towards achieving your goal, rather than in other things.

text: We are absolutely sure of the world. There is no doubt that it exists, but how it exists depends on our instruments of perception.

text: Mindfulness means to be mindful of not only your thoughts but mindful of your emotions and what thoughts come to you when you meet somebody outside.
author: Sri M

text: When the mind is free of distractions then it subsides into its original state and what remains is the purusha - expansive consciousness. In that pure thought, one understands one’s true existence.

text: We are in the same position as Arjuna, in this battlefield of life. We don’t know which way to move. Sometimes we are so overpowered by sorrow, that we don’t know what to do. The music of the Lord, the teachings of Krishna come to save us and pull us out of this mess. This is Bhagavad Gita.
author: Sri M

text: When you are internally mindful, you are also externally mindful. There is no border between the two and in that, you forget even the word mindfulness.
author: Sri M

text: Sit quietly, look at and understand things that you have never seen before. Delve deep into your mind. At the end of this, you may come out like the caterpillar breaks the cocoon and comes out like a colorful butterfly, flying in the skies.
author: Sri M

text: When you live in this world be aware of how you behave. Be mindful of what you do in the outside world, be mindful of your inner world, and one day what will remain is only the witness, the sakshi which is the seer. This is kaivalya .
author: Sri M

text: In the chapter called Yoga of Meditation, “Dhyana Yoga” of Bhagavad Gita, Krishna explains to Arjuna that the mind of a yogi who meditates like a flame is steady even when there is wind. Acquire this capacity through one-pointed attention.
author: Sri M

text: Every morning we see the sunrise. If seeing is believing, then it must be right. But an elementary school kid will tell you that the sun, neither rises nor sets. So how much can I depend on this particular instrument of perception!

text: There are many other parts of the brain that have been left unexplored because so much lopsided interest has been shown in the frontal lobe development. The whole process of yogic sadhana is to awaken these centers, which are normally inactive in us.

text: Not only sadhana is important, but also the practical application of what has been taught, the way of life – dinacharya; what they call in Ayurveda.

text: When you are so deeply continuously in dhyana on the object which is either the deity or your innermost self, after some time you forget that you exist. There is only That. When this stage takes place, it is called Samadhi.

text: If you want to delve deep into the layers of your consciousness and finally reach the essence, then meditation is a must!

text: When you practice the techniques taught through the spiritual texts, you will come to a stage where your mind is no more limited to the brain but is multidimensional.

text: The whole process of life is to go back to that completeness

text: In the middle of the darkness look for a stream of light

text: What seva can you do? Those who are suffering, help them come out of it. And also tell them that ultimately to get free of this suffering, is to find the Truth.

text: If you work for and serve those who are less privileged than you are, that’s the meditation that is required in the outside modern world.

text: When the mind expands, one of the qualities that arises is kindness, and wanting to share what you have experienced.

text: The relationship between each student and the teacher is individual. Something very important to understand otherwise you’ll run into trouble!

text: When a spiritual teacher says something, it’s not the words that are important but the effect it has on you. Something to watch carefully!

text: The only way to find the truth is to take the images out. when the image is out then you see face to face. Until then, we are caught in this.

author: Sri M

text: Jesus said, “real treasure is in your heart where thieves do not break in and steal”. It is this treasure that we should seek.

author: Sri M

text: Those who have transcended the external rites of religion, they should begin to look within to find the true essence. text: What you seek spiritually is right there inside you and we search for it everywhere. The truth is that, in us, in our hearts, there is a beautiful treasure that we always miss.

text: When the limited understands its limitations and then says this is not the way to find it, it becomes quiet. It is only then, there is hope that the other will make itself known.

text: As your feelings become more and more subtle, deeper centers of the human mind open up to form a link to that which is beyond the ordinary mind.

text: Break free from all bondage, realize that your true self is ever free and never bound! This was the clarion call of the great and ancient Upanishadic teaching - Moksha, Moksha, Moksha!

text: The Guru teaches you how to reach this freedom, how to swim towards it, how to enjoy it, how to discover this ocean within you, that the ocean is you. But you don’t know it.

text: That which does not move’ – is that which is absolutely still like the eye of the cyclone, total motion but in the middle, there is no movement – absolute calmness. author: Sri M

text: If I say I know everything, then there is no movement, research, or inquiry. It is what we don’t know that inspires us to seek and move forward.

text: Sharing is an essential part of well-being. As you give, so you receive. So, give whenever possible, whatever possible, in whichever way you can.

author: Sri M

text: Ishavasya Upanishad was a favorite text of Mahatma Gandhi. It begins with a beautiful statement, “Ishavasyam Idam Sarvam” which means that the Supreme being pervades everything here.

text: Each one of us, with our limitations, needs to understand the fact of how we are related to this world, and how, while we are still in this world, can free ourselves from it.

author: Sri M

text: Shivam cannot be touched without the activation of the Shakti. Without the havan kund, no homa can be done.

text: Kali is a symbol of the whole creation. It is the reality – tongue out, blood dripping, this is a reality everywhere you see it happening. Don’t run away from it.

text: Whenever you say Shakti/ energy, in the Indian tradition, it is represented and symbolized as feminine. In the macrocosm, nothing can function without energy. This shakti, fortunately for us, resides in every human being, man or woman, in the form of the Devi known as the Kula-Kundalini Devi.
author: Sri M

text: When the energy in us wakes up, then our consciousness is lifted from the ordinary to the extraordinary. From getting caught up in little, little trinkets, we reach for the treasure. text: Karma yoga - do your work to perfection as much as you can. Don't worry if the results will be good. You have no control over it anyway so, what is the use of spending sleepless nights.
author: Sri M

text: Put your mind and effort into whatever you strive for. If the results don't come, that means somewhere along the line something is not okay. Don't say it is destiny.
author: Sri M

text: Put your effort into what you do. Don't get frustrated, if it does not work immediately. Move forward, study yourself and see that every failure offers an opportunity to move forward, not only in spiritual life but also in material life.
author: Sri M

text: When the river flows, it makes its own boundaries. Nobody makes a boundary for a river.
author: Sri M

text: Do your duties but don’t neglect your spiritual journey. Keep up your duties seriously, so that when you are mature enough, you are freed from it.
author: Sri M

text: Remove all conditioning and remain in that One essential state. This is the aim of the Vedantic teaching.
author: Sri M

text: The function of the Guru is to show a mirror to you. To clean the mirror and show it properly at the right angle so that you see yourself as you actually are, not what you want to be.
author: Sri M

text: The real supreme Guru is the Brahman Himself and not any human being. We have to note this carefully as otherwise the disciple becomes totally dependent on the form of the Guru and not on the state of the Guru.
author: Sri M

text: Kriya is not a magic technique. It’s about how you lead your life, bring about a change in your lifestyle and behaviour. This has to go hand in hand with the practise of Kriya.
author: Sri M

text: My job is to take iron or copper, which is a base metal and try to change it into gold. In a way, you can call me an alchemist, but that formula also requires cooperation from your side.
author: Sri M

text: Everything is inside us, so we need to start by changing ourselves. Otherwise, it is all absolutely wasted!
author: Sri M

text: There is a spark of the divine in every one of us. There is not a single person who doesn’t have this spark. You just need to remove the extra structure. Like a sculptor who sits on a rock, a chisel in one hand and the hammer in the other and chips and chips.
author: Sri M

text: If your mind is considered as a rock and you chip and take away what is unnecessary, Krishna will emerge from your heart. Believe me, every rock has the essence of that Krishna inside. For that, you need to chip away self-importance and your ego. The best way to bring out the positive is by chipping away the negative. Keep chipping.
author: Sri M

text: What is real? The Real is that you are the Self, the inner self. Everything else is role playing. I understand that we need to play the role to perfection but when you finish the photo shoot, don’t forget that you are not what you are projecting but something else.
author: Sri M

text: I’m That which is the essence, a part of the all-pervading Supreme reality. If this thought occurs, then you see the Supreme in every leaf and grain of sand. This has to settle down, absorbed within, and then you see the inner and outer as the same.
author: Sri M

text: Any thought is a distraction during meditation. The only thought that is not a distraction is the thought of the deity or that I am meditating or the thought that in me is the Supreme self. These thoughts are allowed; any other thought is a distraction.
author: Sri M

text: Mouna is a state of mind where the mind has become quiet and tranquil, even in the midst of all cyclones. A human being whose mind has become tranquil can remain peaceful even while talking a lot. So it’s not the external manifestation that is important but the internal state of mind.
author: Sri M

text: Normally, I think I’m already perfect. When I begin to see where I am wrong, what is wrong with me and how to repair myself, it’s then that the whole spiritual journey begins.
author: Sri M

text: Start with where you are. Then you can improve and break the images that you have. Ultimately when you have broken all images, then you find the truth.
author: Sri M

text: ‘That which does not move’ – is that which is absolutely still like the eye of the cyclone, total motion but in the middle there is absolute calmness. And, it is from that calmness that everything is sucked in because it’s a vacuum. And that vacuum ‘– ‘nothingness’ is all powerful.
author: Sri M

text: Greed transfers itself even into the so-called spiritual system. I call this ‘spiritual materialism’. I don’t think real teachers are for sale. You can give a teacher millions of dollars. I don’t think he would teach someone who he thinks is not prepared.
author: Sri M

text: Serving a human being is the greatest form of worship. It also purifies your mind and prepares you for the spiritual journey
author: Sri M

text: Sai Baba of Shirdi was a prime example of a manifestation of the Supreme Being in the form of a poor ‘Fakir’. He taught the unity of not only Vedanta and other Hindu scriptures, but also pointed out that the Essential Reality of all humanity is One! This was the main message of Sai Baba.
author: Sri M

text: Satsang is critical because you ‘become’ according to the company you keep. If I live with people who talk about the Truth or want to find out what it is; who do japa, kirtan and bhajan, then I will become like them. It may take time. If I live with people who are planning which drink to have next, I will become like that. It is but natural.
author: Sri M

text: What each one of us must understand is to first lead a good life - helping as many people as possible, to sing the name of God, to do our ‘japa’, and to dwell on the Inner Spirit constantly.
author: Sri M

text: If both shraddha and saburi are there, then definitely, there is no problem in sadhana. Both are necessary. Absolute, one-pointed total attention is required in our path along with infinite patience.
author: Sri M

text: Every day when you wake up in the morning, or go to bed at night, look at yourself and say, ‘what am I doing? How many falsities are still in my life? Am I really doing my sadhana sincerely?’ People say – I don’t have time. We have time for everything else. The fact is that urgency for sadhana has not arrived.
author: Sri M

text: Spiritual development is not a mass affair. We cannot develop spiritually in groups. All that should be taken off our minds. We are not sheep that can be herded together and made to eat the same food. Spiritual development is an individual affair.
author: Sri M

text: We are either full of our own thoughts or our own prejudices. We are full of what others have taught us or what has been filled into our brain. Usually, there is no space at all! If you are filled to the brim, how can you learn anything? It is not possible.
author: Sri M

text: The Upanishads say that the Truth is something which is far and yet so near; it moves but it’s faster than any movement. It is that which is, and not that which was. Every minute, it is new.
author: Sri M

text: Any place, where the truth is worshipped, is a temple for us. The most important temple is the body. Inside us is the heart where the Truth sits.
author: Sri M

text: The fragrance that you seek is in you. You think it is outside but the good news is that fragrance happens to be your true soul or happiness, your true identity, free of all other distractions.
author: Sri M

text: There is a witness in us who is there in waking, dreaming, and deep sleep, and perhaps the witness himself or herself or itself is the source of the joy and the pain you feel in all the experiences that you go through.
author: Sri M

text: When the mind stops moving in any direction, when it stops, then you understand that which the Upanishads have described as tad dure tad vadantike — it’s so far and it’s so near — within us.
author: Sri M

text: There is prana in all of us and that energy is linked intimately to our thought process. When this energy goes one-pointedly in the direction of the inner, then everything ceases and you go back to your real source which is within us as pure consciousness. Everything else is incidental.
author: Sri M

text: Through bhakti or complete absorption in the divinity, one can reach that inner self.
author: Sri M

text: Either through devotion or through the practice of techniques of yoga, through purifying the mind or understanding the higher levels of Vedanta — depending on who you are, how many lives you have gone through, what you have studied and so on — one day the sleeping energy in us wakes up.
author: Sri M

text: When the mind is free of all distractions, when it settles down, tranquil and quiet, then you find the treasure trove of happiness.
author: Sri M

text: ‘Shakti’ means ultimate, universal, primordial energy. All the energies that we find on this earth are also part of that. It’s a manifestation of that energy.
author: Sri M

text: ​​In the human being, the tremendous energy, after having done its work of making a complete human being, resides quietly, at the bottom of the spine in a centre which we call the ‘muladhara’. ‘Mula’ is root and ‘adhara’ is foundation. So it is the root foundation.
author: Sri M

text: The most intelligent person very soon discovers the limitations of the ordinary intellect. When I say ordinary intellect, it means all the experiences we have in this world come from our five senses.
author: Sri M

text: When the ‘kundalini’ goes to the ‘sahasrara’, then the person has access to wisdom which normally is not possible for the person to acquire, even if he reads a thousand books for a thousand years.
author: Sri M

text: Jesus Christ in the Bible said, ‘Every hill shall be brought low and every valley shall be filled’. So when you are in that stage of low, you should think I am a valley now I am going to be filled at some point. And when I am high up, I must understand that I am a hill, I could be brought down anytime. That balance must be maintained.
author: Sri M

text: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus says, "Blessed are the peacemakers; for they shall be called the children of God. Blessed are the pure in heart; for they shall see God." Jesus was speaking out of his profound spiritual experience that the pure in heart, no matter who they are or where they belong to, shall certainly experience the tremendous being called God, that Supreme Being.
author: Sri M

text: Shankara has written a beautiful commentary on the Principal Upanishads, wherein he says, since the ordinary mind cannot reach That, ordinary knowledge is of no use to find the truth. Intelligence and knowledge appear when one understands this fact. Then one has knowledge.
author: Sri M

text: The awakening and movement of the energy is also an unconditioning of the little self. When it reaches the ‘sahasrara’, the little self is blasted in pieces and there is only the real Self.
author: Sri M

text: When Adi Shankara says knowledge, he is talking about that knowledge which cannot be found through the sense organs, that which cannot be processed by the brain.
author: Sri M

text: I see the whole world with my eyes but I can’t see my own eyes. I can’t turn around and look at my own eyes but when I see in the mirror, I know that I have eyes. In the same way That awareness is a witness to everything.
author: Sri M

text: The first step to self-realisation is to realise that this self as I know it is cluttered and that this clutter needs to be removed.
author: Sri M

text: As far as the body is concerned the most important thing is that there should be no excesses. In the Gita, Krishna beautifully defines it. He says this yoga is not for him who eats too much or eats too little, or sleeps too much or sleeps too little. It’s a metaphor which means stick to the middle path.
author: Sri M
